title: Business Operations & Productivity
summary: P4 builds the workbooks that run a business day to day: forms, trackers, rosters and schedules, stock, sales and invoices, attendance and payroll, made so other people can use them without breaking them.
prereq: Builds on C1 · Excel Foundations and C2 · Formulas & Functions (lookups, dates, COUNTIFS and SUMIFS). P2’s conditional formatting helps in Modules 2 and 3.
outcomes: Design workbooks other people can fill in without breaking: clear inputs, validation, protection and templates.
Plan with working calendars, rotating shift rosters, project schedules and Gantt charts.
Build trackers and logs that flag what’s overdue and summarise status at a glance.
Run stock: ledgers, reorder points, ABC analysis and stock valuation.
Handle orders and invoices: price lookups, GST, commission slabs and receivables ageing.
Keep people records: the employee master, attendance, leave balances and attrition.
Prepare payroll from attendance: salary structures, example deductions, payslips and the register.
Share, collect, print and hand over workbooks so they keep working.

modules.title: Workbooks people can’t break
modules.summary: Designing for other users, validation that guides (dependent lists and custom rules), protection that works, and templates and logs.

lessons.title: Designing for other people
lessons.summary: A workbook other people fill in is a small product. Give it one place to type, labels that say the unit, rules kept in cells, and checks that tell the user what’s missing.
objectives: Separate inputs, calculations and outputs, and colour-code them so users know where to type.
Put units in labels and rules in cells, never inside formulas.
Flag missing fields with IF and COUNTBLANK, and show a status line.
Test a form the way a user will, including wrong entries.

lessons.summary: Data validation stops bad entries at the door: drop-down lists from named ranges, dependent lists with INDIRECT, custom rules for duplicates and limits, and messages that tell people what’s allowed.

lessons.title: Protection that works
lessons.summary: Lock everything but the inputs, hide formulas you don’t want edited, let people sort and filter, give different people different cells, and know what protection can’t do.
objectives: Unlock the input cells and protect the sheet, choosing what people may still do.
Hide formulas from the formula bar, and protect the workbook’s structure.
Use Allow Edit Ranges to give different people different cells.
Avoid the gotchas: Tables on protected sheets, sorting and filtering, and protection that isn’t security.

lessons.title: Templates and logs
lessons.summary: A form is filled in many times; a log collects every record in one list. Save forms as templates, keep logs as Tables with one row per record, and summarise them with COUNTIF, SUMIFS and AVERAGE.
objectives: Keep a log as a Table: one row per record, no blank rows, summaries off to the side.
Make IDs with TEXT, freeze them as values, and work out days between dates with IF for blanks.
Summarise a log with COUNTIF, SUMIFS and AVERAGE.
Save a form as a template (.xltx) and decide between a template and a shared log.
topics: IDs and dates that don’t change
What goes in a good template

modules.title: Calendars, rosters and schedules
modules.summary: Working days with WORKDAY.INTL and a holiday list, rotating shift rosters, project schedules with dependencies, and Gantt charts.
modules.testInfo: Working days, rosters, schedules and Gantt charts

lessons.title: Working calendars
lessons.summary: Customers count calendar days; factories count working days. WORKDAY.INTL and NETWORKDAYS.INTL skip your weekly off and a named holiday list, so promises and counts match the real calendar.
objectives: Add working days to a date with WORKDAY.INTL, skipping the weekly off and a holiday list.
Choose the weekend argument: 1 for Saturday and Sunday, 11 for Sunday only, or a seven-character pattern.
Count working days between dates with NETWORKDAYS.INTL.
Flag late dispatches and work out an on-time rate.
topics: A holiday list with a name

lessons.title: Shift rosters
lessons.summary: A roster is a calendar with a rule. Build the dates once with SEQUENCE, then let MOD rotate three teams through morning, evening and night shifts, with Sundays off and a check that every night is covered.
objectives: Build a row of dates with SEQUENCE, with day names (TEXT) and week numbers.
Rotate teams through shifts with MOD and INDEX, giving each team an offset.
Mark the weekly off with WEEKDAY.
Check cover and fairness with COUNTIF.
topics: A row of dates in one formula
The weekly off and the checks

lessons.title: Project schedules
lessons.summary: A schedule is a list of tasks, each with a duration in working days and the task it waits for. Finish dates come from WORKDAY.INTL, start dates from the task before, so when one task slips every later date moves by itself.
objectives: Lay out a schedule: ID, task, working days, the task it follows, start and finish.
Work out finish dates with WORKDAY.INTL (days − 1), with milestones of 0 days.
Link each start to the finish of the task before with XLOOKUP, looking only above to avoid circular references.
See the effect of a slip, and handle tasks that wait for two others.

lessons.title: Gantt charts
lessons.summary: A Gantt chart shows a schedule as bars on a calendar. Build it on the sheet with a SEQUENCE date row and one conditional formatting rule, add a status-date line, or draw it as a stacked bar chart for slides.
objectives: Lay out a Gantt grid: tasks down, a SEQUENCE row of dates across.
Draw the bars with a formula rule, =AND(E$4>=$B5,E$4<=$C5), locking the right row and columns.
Add a status-date line and shade the weekly off, and order the rules.
Make a Gantt as a stacked bar chart, and choose between the two.
topics: Status line, weekly off and rule order

modules.title: Trackers
modules.summary: Task trackers with due dates and checkboxes, status at a glance with COUNTIFS and RAG colours, and request logs with ageing.
modules.testInfo: Task trackers, status summaries and request logs

lessons.title: Task trackers
lessons.summary: A tracker lists what has to be done, by whom and by when, and says by itself what’s late. Checkboxes hold TRUE and FALSE, a status formula reads the dates, and conditional formatting colours the rows that need attention.
objectives: Lay out a tracker: task, owner, due date, done, status.
Use checkboxes (TRUE or FALSE) in formulas.
Work out a status with nested IF or IFS from an as-of date, and the days late.
Colour whole rows with a formula rule, and summarise progress.

lessons.title: Status at a glance
lessons.summary: A manager reads a summary, not 12 rows. Count statuses by owner with COUNTIFS, turn the counts into a red, amber or green rating, and keep a live list of what’s late with FILTER.
objectives: Build an owner-by-status matrix with one COUNTIFS formula and mixed references.
Turn counts into a RAG rating with rules written down.
Show the share done per owner.
Keep a live list of overdue tasks with FILTER.
topics: A live list of what’s late

lessons.title: Request logs and ageing
lessons.summary: A request log records every job that comes in: when it was raised, how urgent it is, and when it was closed. Age, service levels and age bands turn the log into a list of what needs chasing.
objectives: Work out the age of open and closed requests from an as-of date.
Look up a service level (SLA) by priority, and flag requests past it.
Put open requests into age bands with an approximate XLOOKUP.
Summarise a log with COUNTIFS and MAXIFS on blank cells.
topics: Age bands with an approximate lookup

modules.title: Stock and inventory
modules.summary: Item masters and stock ledgers, reorder points and safety stock, ABC analysis, and valuing and ageing stock.

lessons.title: Item masters and stock ledgers
lessons.summary: Stock is two lists: an item master that says what each item is, and a ledger that records every movement in and out. Balances are worked out from the ledger, never typed.
objectives: Keep an item master with a unique code per item, and look items up by code.
Record every movement in a ledger, with In and Out turned into signed quantities.
Work out a running balance per item with an expanding SUMIFS.
Work out stock now from the opening stock and the ledger.

lessons.title: Reorder points and safety stock
lessons.summary: Order too late and the shelves run empty; order too early and cash sits in the store. The reorder point says when to order: enough stock to last the supplier’s lead time, plus a safety buffer.
objectives: Work out safety stock from average daily use and safety days.
Work out the reorder point: use during the lead time plus safety stock.
Flag items to order, and show days of cover.
Round an order up to whole packs with CEILING.MATH.

lessons.title: ABC analysis
lessons.summary: A few items carry most of the value. ABC analysis sorts items by the value they use a year, adds up their shares, and labels them A, B or C, so you watch the A items closely and keep the C items simple.
objectives: Work out each item’s value used a year, and sort the items largest first.
Work out each item’s share and the running (cumulative) share.
Label items A, B or C from cumulative-share rules kept in cells.
Summarise the share of items and of value in each class.
topics: A few items carry most of the value

lessons.title: Valuing and ageing stock
lessons.summary: Stock is money on shelves. Value it at a weighted average cost, see how long each item has sat without moving, and set aside a provision for stock that may never sell.
objectives: Work out a weighted average cost per item from its receipts with SUMIFS.
Value the stock on hand.
Age stock by days since it last moved, and band it with an approximate lookup.
Work out a provision for slow and non-moving stock, and total value by band.

modules.title: Sales and invoicing
modules.summary: Order registers and price lookups, GST invoices, commission slabs and targets, and receivables ageing.

lessons.title: Order registers and price lookups
lessons.summary: An order register lists every order line. Prices, customer types and discounts come from lookup tables, so nobody types a price, and a price change is one cell on the price list.
objectives: Keep a price list and a customer list, and look values up by code and name.
Look up a price in a two-way table: the item’s row and the customer type’s column.
Apply a volume discount from quantity breaks with an approximate XLOOKUP.
Total sales by customer type with SUMIFS.

lessons.title: GST invoices
lessons.summary: A tax invoice lists each item’s taxable value and the GST on it. Within your own state the tax splits into CGST and SGST; to another state it’s IGST. Lookups bring in the rates, and one IF decides which tax applies.
objectives: Lay out a tax invoice: invoice number, date, customer, place of supply, lines and totals.
Look up each line’s GST rate and work out the taxable value.
Split GST into CGST and SGST for an intra-state sale, or IGST for an inter-state one, with IF.
Total the invoice and round it to the rupee.
topics: The parts of a tax invoice

lessons.title: Commission slabs and targets
lessons.summary: Sales teams are paid on results. Measure each rep against target, pick a commission rate from achievement bands, compare it with a tiered scheme like income-tax slabs, and cap the payout.
objectives: Work out achievement against target as a percentage.
Pick a commission rate from achievement bands with an approximate XLOOKUP.
Work out a tiered (slab) commission with SUMPRODUCT and an extra-rate column.
Cap a payout with MIN, and count reps at target.

lessons.title: Receivables ageing
lessons.summary: Sales aren’t cash until customers pay. An ageing report works out each invoice’s due date and balance, how many days it’s overdue, and which bucket it falls in, so the oldest money gets chased first.
objectives: Work out due dates from credit terms, and balances from receipts.
Work out days overdue against an as-of date, zero for invoices not yet due.
Put invoices into ageing buckets (not due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+).
Total balances by bucket and work out the share overdue more than 60 days.

modules.title: People: attendance and leave
modules.summary: The employee master, attendance registers, leave balances, and headcount and attrition.
modules.testInfo: Employee records, attendance, leave and attrition

lessons.title: The employee master
lessons.summary: Every people workbook starts with one list: an ID, name, department and joining date for each employee. Service, probation dates, status and email addresses are worked out from it, and every other sheet looks people up by ID.
objectives: Keep an employee master with a unique ID per person, looked up everywhere else.
Work out years of service and “3 y 4 m” with DATEDIF.
Work out probation end dates with EDATE and a status from the as-of date.
Build email addresses with text functions, and count people by department.

lessons.title: Attendance registers
lessons.summary: An attendance register is a grid: people down, days across, one code per cell. COUNTIF turns the codes into days present, on leave and absent, and absent days decide the paid days that payroll uses.
objectives: Lay out a monthly attendance grid with codes from a drop-down list.
Show day names with TEXT, and grey out weekly offs and holidays.
Count present, leave and absent days with COUNTIF, counting half days as 0.5.
Work out paid days for payroll, and highlight absences with conditional formatting.

lessons.title: Leave balances
lessons.summary: Leave is a running account: brought forward, plus credits, minus what’s taken. Count each application in working days, add them up per person and type with SUMIFS, and flag anyone who has taken more than they have.
objectives: Count the working days in a leave application with NETWORKDAYS.INTL and the holiday list.
Total leave taken per person and type with SUMIFS on another sheet.
Work out balances: brought forward + credited − taken.
Flag over-drawn balances with IF and OR.

lessons.title: Headcount and attrition
lessons.summary: How many people work here, who joined, who left, and how fast people leave. With joining and leaving dates on one list, COUNTIFS gives the headcount on any date, the joiners and leavers each month, and the attrition rate.
objectives: Count headcount on a date with COUNTIFS on joining and leaving dates.
Count joiners and leavers in each month between two month ends.
Work out average headcount and the monthly attrition rate.
Work out attrition for the year, and check that the numbers add up.
topics: Who was here on a date?
Joiners and leavers in a month

modules.title: Payroll
modules.summary: Salary structures, deductions with example rates, and payslips and the payroll register.

lessons.title: Salary structures
lessons.summary: A monthly salary is split into parts: basic, house rent allowance, conveyance and a special allowance that makes up the rest. Rules in cells turn each gross salary into its parts, and the employer’s PF turns it into the cost to the company.
objectives: Split a monthly gross salary into basic, HRA, conveyance and a balancing special allowance.
Keep the structure’s rules in cells, and round each part to the rupee.
Work out the employer’s PF with a wage ceiling, using MIN.
Work out cost to company (CTC) for the year.

lessons.title: Deductions
lessons.summary: From gross to take-home: pay for the days worked, then deduct the employee’s PF, ESI and professional tax. Every rate, limit and slab sits in a cell, because they change; this lesson’s are examples.
objectives: Pro-rate pay for paid days from the attendance register.
Work out the employee’s PF with a ceiling, and ESI only for those under the gross limit, rounded up.
Look up professional tax from a slab table.
Work out total deductions and net pay.

lessons.title: Payslips and the register
lessons.summary: The payroll register is the month’s record: one row per person, totals that tie. A payslip is a view of one row: pick an Emp ID, and lookups fill in the rest. Then the money moves only when the totals check out.
objectives: Keep a payroll register with totals and a zero-check.
Build a payslip that fills itself from the register by Emp ID.
Use one two-way XLOOKUP for every payslip line, matching row labels to register headings.
Put the month-end payroll steps in order.

modules.title: Sharing and running a workbook
modules.summary: Co-authoring and comments, collecting data with Forms and imports, printing forms and payslips, and handing a workbook over.

lessons.title: Co-authoring and comments
lessons.summary: A workbook kept on OneDrive or SharePoint can be edited by several people at once. Share it with the right access, talk in comments and @mentions instead of email, and use version history when something goes wrong.
objectives: Share a workbook from OneDrive or SharePoint with edit or view access, instead of emailing copies.
Know what co-authoring needs: a cloud file, AutoSave, and a current version of Excel.
Use threaded comments and @mentions; know how they differ from notes.
Restore an earlier version with version history.

lessons.title: Collecting data with Forms and imports
lessons.summary: Data that people type into a form, or that arrives as a file, needs tidying before it’s used. Microsoft Forms keeps entries consistent; imports bring files in; TRIM, PROPER, VALUE and DATE clean what arrives, and a duplicate check catches double entries.
objectives: Collect entries with a Microsoft Form whose responses land in Excel, using choices and required questions.
Import a file with Data › Get Data, and refresh it next time.
Clean names, text numbers and text dates with TRIM, PROPER, VALUE and DATE.
Flag duplicate entries with COUNTIFS on a growing range, and summarise without them.

lessons.title: Printing forms and payslips
lessons.summary: Some workbooks end on paper or as a PDF: payslips, invoices, the stores count sheet. Set the print area, fit the page, repeat headings on every page, add a footer, and save PDFs with names that say what they are.
objectives: Set a print area and fit a form to one page.
Repeat heading rows on every printed page with Print Titles.
Add headers and footers with page numbers and the file name.
Save a payslip as a PDF, with a file name built by a formula.

lessons.title: Handing a workbook over
lessons.summary: A workbook is finished when someone else can run it without you. Give it a Read me sheet, checks that say whether it’s healthy, clean names and structure, and inspect it before it leaves the building.
objectives: Write a Read me sheet: purpose, owner, monthly steps, inputs and version.
Build checks that run themselves: count errors with SUMPRODUCT(--ISERROR()), blanks with COUNTBLANK, and an overall status with AND.
Fix what the checks find.
Inspect the document and check accessibility before sharing outside.

project.title: An operations workbook for Rakshak Safety Gear
project.brief: A month of orders, stock movements and attendance for a safety-gear maker: build a protected workbook with a stock ledger and reorder alerts, an invoice register with GST and ageing, and attendance feeding payroll, ready for the team to use.
